scope: Existing 39368295521 and 39369947381 receipts and original-run profiles only; no workflow dispatch or repository mutation by this analysis.
findings: Original failure coincides with 95% host CPU nonidle and sustained driver queue overflow; three-node product CPU is the major measured consumer, and driver decoding also consumes meaningful CPU.
No persisted-read admission refusal observed; all sampled occupancy values <=8 with limit16. Driver drops are discarded benchmark arrivals, not lost product messages.
Matched candidate has ~47.3%/~63.2% greater list/sync median window P99 and only ~2ms driver wait. Request spans HTTP, decode, validation and scheduling, not pure server time.

Matched mean server handlers are also ~21.2%/~19.8% slower; same stage/call counts and +0.011% allocation do not support a large increase in work or allocations. CPU/request +2.83% and driver ticks/request +4.66%.
Raw stage buckets absent; server P99 cannot be reconstructed from sums/counts. CPU, wall-time stages and independent P99 fields are not additive.
Original 7763 vs matched9V45 also differ in completion mix and recorded RPC fanout, so model alone is not an isolated causal variable.

Profiles are separate later windows, not original 60s windows. Server samples begin before warmup and cover only ~7.36s of measured10s. Matching profile-window ranking reverses, so they cannot prove original tail regression.
next_experiment: One predeclared reversed-order same-host pair (b469 then beta24) using frozen b469 harness/profile. Root manages exact build-provenance digest locks and preserves any pre-measurement failures; this analysis does not dispatch or declare its result.
